A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic-regex research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-description benchmarks, consistency and complexity analyses, and a 24-participant user study in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a GPT-4o versus GPT-4o-mini ablation on 520 features in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The semantic-regex primitives, modifiers, substantive prompting instructions, and generation pipeline remain unchanged. The new grounded-theory account explains the existing language's development; substituting GPT-4o is an evaluation ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GPT-2 and Gemma-2 SAE features using OpenWebText and Pile Uncopyrighted activations, alongside the same user-study population and tasks. The added ablation uses existing GPT-2 coverage with another explainer/evaluator configuration.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators remain token-act-pair and max-acts, and the user study retains max-acts. The new ablation evaluates the same three description methods without introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a matched comparison on 520 randomly sampled GPT-2 features, substituting GPT-4o for GPT-4o-mini in both explanation and evaluation while retaining prompts and activation formatting. It evaluates five generation/discrimination metrics; the original experiments' settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds the first systematic sensitivity analysis of dependence on explainer/evaluator capability, comparing both models across all three description methods and five metrics (Appendix C, Table A2, Figures A2–A3). This introduces a substantive robustness question absent from v1. Appendix D also extends the existing cost analysis to GPT-4o.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the one-sided paired non-inferiority test with a 5% margin, Bonferroni correction for superiority, and existing dispersion reporting. The ablation uses the established mean ± standard deviation practice; no new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds ablation results and GPT-4o cost estimates while retaining Table A1 and the original plotted benchmark and user-study values. In new Table A2, semantic-regex responsiveness is 0.84 under both models, whereas token-act-pair changes from 0.83 with GPT-4o-mini to 0.90 with GPT-4o, reversing their ranking. These are newly reported experimental conditions, not improvements over v1's main benchmark.

T1.justification: The language-component definitions and cost equation remain substantively unchanged. The added design rationale and conceptual qualifications introduce no new mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: structured feature descriptions with comparable accuracy, greater conciseness and consistency, complexity analysis, and benefits for human interpretation. The added ablation supports existing claims rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands limitations beyond v1's discussion of overly terse descriptions, addressing non-uniqueness, underspecified matching, polysemanticity, grammatical errors, and evaluation validity. Appendix E explicitly frames the user study as qualitative. Appendix C also adds a model-robustness interpretation, although its claim of unchanged relative performance overstates Table A2.

D1.justification: v1 promises code and a demo; v2 reports their availability and supplies access locations. Appendix E newly documents the detection-score threshold above 75%, manual verification, and layer/component composition of the existing study features. Section 3.1 explains language-development provenance, while the detailed implementation tables and prompts are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Corbin and Strauss on grounded theory, Kopf et al. on PRISM and polysemanticity, and van Rossum et al. on style guidelines, while removing Lipton's interpretability reference. These provide targeted methodological and limitation context without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, corrects terminology and prompt-listing typos, and expands explanations while retaining the main narrative. It inserts discussion, ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements and reorganizes the appendices, including moving the existing cost analysis earlier.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ablation table and two plots, extends the cost table, reverses the display order of Figure A1 and Table A1, and makes localized figure corrections and resizing. Existing benchmark graphics and survey screenshots are retained; the overall single-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 improves transparency through explicit failure conditions, fuller user-study selection details, and reported code access, while adding a useful model-capability check. The gain is limited by overinterpretation of that check: Table A2 contains ranking reversals despite the claim that relative performance is unchanged. The clearer documentation and limitations nevertheless support a modest net improvement.
